scopeChanges.text: M0 includes the import of the Pagewing core (no UI) from the `v1.0.0` tag as the project skeleton: unchanged import, scripted rename, a commit that makes the subset self-contained, and the translation of German text. The listed tasks for the skeleton, `.gitignore` and CI are carried out on top of the imported solution. `.env.example` is not needed because the imported code uses no secrets. Decided in the suite spec and in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` (entry "Core-only import, fresh UI, new order of work").

Localized key names in menu shortcuts (`Strg+X` instead of `Ctrl+X`) and the TextBox context menu strings (Fluent's English Cut, Copy and Paste) move to milestone 1.2 with the German layout work. The gallery window is 1520 x 900. Decisions in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entries "Shell project and token conventions (M1.1)" and "Localization mechanism and its limits". The high-contrast palette is a fixed palette, not a token set built from the system colours as the spec asks (entry "High-contrast palette"); owner to confirm.
AppFrame collapses an empty tab row and band, so the start view sits directly under the title bar; the gallery's frame demo gets a fifth File tab.
`AutomationNameTests` ignores the RepeatButtons inside a RangeBase (the zoom slider), which carry no name of their own.
`RibbonView.NotifyInvoked` is new so that `CommandInvoked` also fires for commands run by a field code.

Additions beyond the plan, needed by the frame demo and the reviews: `Pane.IsDocument` and `Pane.PaneName`, `AppFrame.IsLeftPaneShown` and `IsRightPaneShown`, `TitleBar.LeadingInset`, zoom from 10 to 500 percent in steps of 10 with snapping, `FieldCodeTarget`, `PaneFocus.Focus(Pane)` and `StartView.FocusFirstTile`.

Q (search), 6 and 7 (panes) act in the field-code tab-letter stage through app-supplied `FieldCodeTarget`s; the spec lists the badges as display only and the plan said "shows". The group digits stay a display-only legend.

The frame demo window has a minimum width of 1024 px. The full ribbon at 1024 px without the compact bar clips groups of the Home tab; this is a recorded limitation and not a tested case, there is no automatic compact mode (backlog).

The shell tests run serially (`DisableTestParallelization` in `tests/Raffica.Shell.Tests/TestCulture.cs`) because parallel test classes switching the shared `ShellStrings.Culture` made the suite flaky (about one first run in three after a build).

Milestones 2.1 to 2.6 are added under the PDF spec: Viewer, Annotate, Forms and signing, Organize pages, Redact, OCR and line editing, Packaging and release. Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entries "Raffica PDF: scope and order (M2)" and "Raffica PDF: speed budgets are measured, not inherited (M2)".
Milestone 3 (macOS spec) now depends on 2.6 instead of 2, so that macOS stays after the finished PDF app; milestone 2 only means that the PDF spec exists.

The OCR library build moves from the backlog into milestone 2.5, and the release workflow into 2.6; the CodeQL and hardware-measure workflows come back in 2.5. Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: platform code, autosave, OCR build and releases (M2)".

Milestone 2.1 adds an additive option to the shell's settings dialog so that the PDF app hides the autosave row (autosave contradicts "never damages the original"); the frame's behaviour for the other apps stays as it is. Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: platform code, autosave, OCR build and releases (M2)".

Inventory of Pagewing 1.0 (its roadmap and README at the `v1.0.0` tag), entered as marks `(P<n>)` in the tasks of 2.1 to 2.6. Done in 2.1 although not named in the spec's list: document info from the status bar (P4: file, pages, page size, PDF version, file size, metadata) and the F1 help card with the shortcut overview built from the command catalog (P6). Already done in the imported core: `raffica search` (P5). Open for after 2.6 unless the owner asks earlier, both in the backlog: tabs between windows (P4.1) and the "open in new window" command of P4, because the frame's `DocumentTabs` has no drag-out and a workspace across windows is a shell feature that no other app needs yet; the setting "reduce animations" (P6), because the shell's design spec has no such setting and its motion is limited to control transitions (owner to confirm). Not rebuilt on purpose: the density setting (replaced by the compact command bar of the shell) and a separate high-contrast switch (Pagewing followed the system setting as well, and the shell does the same through `ShellTheme.Apply`, so there is nothing to rebuild). Pagewing's public-repository work (12.1) is the owner's decision and stays listed as open in 2.6.

Three additive extensions of the shell, needed by the PDF app and neutral for the other apps: (1) the settings dialog takes optional `SettingsDialogOptions` (hide the autosave row, extra rows the app builds and reads in its `onOk`), (2) `DocumentTab` gets a dirty marker and an exposed selected state (the selected state of document tabs for assistive technology is done with it, and the backlog item "Accessibility items deferred from the frame" is narrowed to what remains), (3) the frame's `SearchField` takes an optional `ExtraResults` provider for entries that are not ribbon commands (open tabs, recent files, outline entries, "Go to page N"). Decided in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: viewer conventions (M2.1)".
A file that is already open is selected, not opened twice (Pagewing opened a second tab). Two tabs of one file would both hold dirty state once 2.2 adds editing.
The test PDF generator of Pagewing (`tools/make-testpdfs.cs`) is not imported in 2.1: the fixtures under `testdata/pdfs` cover every viewer test, and a task that needs a new fixture says so.

Milestone 2.1 has 17 tasks in its plan. If the owner asks, it can be split after Task 11 of the plan into 2.1 (viewing and searching) and a further milestone (printing and speed budgets); the extra id is chosen then.

Additions to the shell made while building 2.1, neutral for the other apps: the status bar zoom range goes up to 800 percent (it was 500; Core allows 800, and above 500 the buttons and the slider drove the zoom backwards), and `CommandDefinition` gets `EnabledWhen` and `DisabledReason` so that a ribbon command can be disabled with a reason (`RibbonView.RefreshCommandStates`; the ribbon did not disable commands before).

The Home tab of the PDF ribbon grew to 7 groups and 29 commands (Close tab, Settings, Tabs, Text and Help groups were added); the spec leaves the ribbon content to the app within the frame rules. With no document open, Open, Help and Settings are enabled (the plan said only Open).
The Linux print card has no paper-size row: Core's `PrintSettings` has no paper field (the same as Pagewing 1.0), so the printer's default paper is used. The plan item "paper size" is not delivered.
The settings of PDF follow Core's enums: the page appearance reads "Light / Follow theme" and the default zoom offers three modes (Free is not a valid default).

`--settings-file` isolates all of the app's files (`pdf-settings.json` and `recent.json` next to the given file) and the single-instance pipe (its name gets a hash suffix of the path), so a measurement or a test never touches the user's data.

A file given on the command line at first launch opens at the default position, not at the remembered one: `recent.json` is loaded only after the first sharp page. Measured option for a follow-up: read it in parallel on a pool thread during the open (about 2 ms per run, no effect on the first page); recommended, not adopted. Recorded in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.
Naming hygiene: four comments and notes under `bench/` that named the predecessor are reworded to "the predecessor"; the tests keep "Pagewing" only as test data.

Milestone 2.1 is closed `done` although acceptance criterion 3 (manual check: a file passed as argument and a second file in the running instance) was not checked: the owner skipped it on 2026-11-04. The criterion stays unticked, the automated paths are covered by tests (`InstanceHandoverTests`, `HandoverWindowTests`, `OpenFlowTests`), and the manual check is a backlog entry. The task "Set the PDF speed budgets" is ticked although Chrome was not measured again on the two machines (the M1 numbers stand) and the Windows start-time finding was still open (resolved on 2026-11-04, see the next entry).

Software rendering is the Windows default of the PDF app (owner decision of 2026-11-04, after the measurement of runs 41892985596 and 41893002871: every start case halves, idle memory drops to a third, the scroll p99 rises from 13.5 to 18.0 ms). `RAFFICA_RENDERING=default` opts out; Linux and macOS are untouched. The Windows budgets of the PDF target are re-derived from the software medians (cold 200, warm 210, 1000 pages 200, second file 20, scroll p99 20 ms, memory 40, size 51, zip 22 MiB; the old ones, 400/390/400/30/20 ms and 130 MiB, belonged to the GPU path); the Linux budgets stand. Entry "Raffica PDF: software rendering is the Windows default (M2.1 follow-up)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.

The right pane of the PDF app is one marks pane of 256 px (the approved canvas shows a single pane "Markierungen" and no separate comments pane); the empty 300 px comments pane slot of 2.1 is reused for it, and a mark's comment is shown and edited in its entry. The annotate mode of the predecessor is kept (a tool in the Annotate tab starts it, Esc or "Done" ends it); comments are the `/Contents` of a markup or drawing. Not rebuilt from the predecessor's 1.0 feature set because Core has no support for them: sticky notes, reply threads, shape fill, pressure-sensitive width, and a full-rewrite option for annotation saves (annotation saves are incremental only). Entry "Raffica PDF: annotation conventions (M2.2)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`; owner to confirm the marks pane.

Changes while building, against the plan and the entry "Raffica PDF: annotation conventions (M2.2)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` (amended there): (a) the tool letters I, R, E, L, A and T are not implemented; the Annotate tab's key tips and the Ctrl+Shift shortcuts exist instead, which avoids another key-capture surface. (b) Colour and width are chosen in an app-side style strip (`Annotating/StyleStrip`) beside the mode badge, not in the ribbon, because the shell ribbon has no checked or swatch control; moving it into the ribbon is a later option. A text box gets colours only on the strip, for a selection. (c) The text-box default font size is 16 pt (Medium, the default of Core and Pagewing 1.0); the plan text said 12. (d) The ribbon shows no checked state for the active tool; the mode badge names the tool and "Esc to finish". (e) Touch input is ignored in annotate mode, because the page view has no touch scrolling yet. (f) The marks pane (256 px, the one right pane) stays flagged "owner to confirm".

Departures from the predecessor's forms and signature designs (M11, M12), approved by the owner on 2026-11-05: (1) there is no separate "Fill form" mode; form fields are live whenever the document has fillable fields and no annotate tool is active, and an annotate tool makes them inert. (2) The field highlight is a per-tab switch on a form badge (on by default for a document with fillable fields, not stored); PDFium draws it, the app draws stars for required and locks for read-only fields and the focus ring. (3) The required-field card before saving stays ("Go to first empty field" is the default, "Save anyway" never blocks) and gets a counter on the badge and a "Next required field" command. (4) The notices (calculations and format scripts, XFA, signature fields, buttons) are one dismissible line naming only what applies, not one bar per hint. (5) Core gets `PdfDocument.MayFillFormsAsync` with a Core test, because `MayAnnotateAsync` alone would lock forms of documents that allow only filling. (6) Signing is one step: the Sign command opens the New-signature card when nothing is saved, else a picker card with thumbnails; a pick is placed in the centre of the visible part of the page and selected with the select tool (no ghost under the pointer). Not rebuilt: renaming a saved signature, pasting an image from the clipboard. The signatures folder lies next to `--settings-file` when that switch is given. Entry "Raffica PDF: forms and signing conventions (M2.3)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.

Changes while building, against the plan (details in the amendment of the entry "Raffica PDF: forms and signing conventions (M2.3)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`). Core got four small additions: `PdfDocument.MayFillFormsAsync`, the `GetFormFieldsAsync(int, PdfPriority, ...)` overload, `AnnotationEditor.HasFormChanges` and `PngEncoder.EncodeWithAlpha`. The required-field card is asked for any form change (`HasFormChanges`, which stays true until the next save clears the history, also after the only form step was undone); the form-aware signed-file wording stays tied to `HasOnlyFormChanges`. Every field-editor text box has `AcceptsReturn = true` and no `MaxLength` (the inner text box of an editable combo box keeps Avalonia's default, see the open items), so Avalonia never shortens a pasted text; a pasted break is refused with the one-line hint, instead of the planned `MaxLength` from the field. Added beyond the plan: hover tooltips and composed automation names for locked and required widgets (`FormInteraction`, `FormAutomation`), `FormFocus.PageToLoad` (the walk never jumps an unloaded page, failed page reads are remembered), non-focusable badge buttons, a card when the signature library cannot be read, the Sign group (digit 5, code 51), image signatures that can be moved and scaled (`SelectController.CanChange` tests `SelectionShape`) and Cancel disabled while a signature save is in flight. `NativeBindingsTests` was fixed: `PermissionFillForms` is a PDF-specification bit and is mapped in `SpecificationValues`.

Departures from the predecessor's page design (M13) and the author's calls of the plan `superpowers/plans/2026-11-05-milestone-02-4-organize-pages.md`, recorded in `Docs/DECISIONS.md` ("Raffica PDF: page organizing conventions (M2.4)"); the owner can overturn single calls: (1) while a page plan is open, the annotate tools, Sign, form filling, Extract, Split and Export images are disabled with the reason "Apply or discard the page changes first" (the output commands read the open document without the plan). (2) Unsaved marks or form values are saved first, after a question; flowing the history into the working copy is not built. (3) The Apply card offers "Save as…" as the default and "Save in the original file" as an armed second choice, lists every loss per kind before anything is written, and says that a rewrite cannot be undone and that no backup copy is made. (4) After a rewrite the app rebuilds the view and panes of the tab (fallback: reopen the written file in the same strip position), because the page list and the page sizes changed. (5) Merge is "Insert file…" into the plan with a page range and a position; the predecessor's merge dialog with a file list stays in the backlog. (6) Extract, Split and Export images are cards with a range field that read the open document; JPEG, crop, watermark, page numbers, page labels, images as pages and dragging pages between tabs stay out as in the predecessor. (7) The ribbon gets a Pages tab (letter P) with the organize, edit, history, apply, output and destructive groups. Milestone 2.5 (redaction) builds on the same rewrite mechanics and the tab rebuild.

Changes while building, against the plan (details in the amendment of the entry "Raffica PDF: page organizing conventions (M2.4)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`): the organize mode itself counts as a plan open (also with an identity plan) and locks the annotate tools, Sign, form clicks, keys and commands, marks-pane comments and the output commands; a running save, extract, split or export locks the page commands and the other way round; Save and Save as with a changed plan hand over to the Apply flow through a delegate of `SaveController`; the analysis and rewrite job cards are modal and Apply, Extract, Split and Export images share one `JobRunner` class; closing or discarding a changed plan asks with its own card, and unsaved marks are asked afterwards (a Cancel keeps the plan); the plan version is re-checked before the write; at most 20 files can be inserted per organize session (every registered file counts); a file without pages is refused as unreadable; no `BlankPageCard` was built (a blank page takes the size of its neighbour). Added to earlier code: `OrganizeSession.Ending`, `OrganizeSession.Summarize`, `PdfTab.OrganizeCreated`, `PdfWindow.RebuildTab` and `PdfTab.ResetForRewrittenDocument`. Open: the manual check in an independent viewer and the points in the "Open items" block of milestone 2.4.

The ribbon gets two tabs: Redact (letter R, with the destructive group last) and Edit (letter E: edit text lines, recognize text, language files); the right pane shows the redact pane in the marks-pane slot while the mode is on. Pattern search names picture pages and offers OCR, it never starts it. The OCR run is not modal: an options card starts it, a run badge and the status bar show progress with Cancel, a finished run is one unsaved history step. Redaction cleanup stays "not a switch" (owner, 2026-11-06). The OCR library is built here by a dispatch-only workflow on hosted runners and published as the prerelease `native-tesseract-5.5.4-1` of this repository (running it is an owner gate); because the repository is private, `tools/native-fetch.cs` reads the release assets through the GitHub API with a token and keeps the pinned size and SHA-256 as the trust anchor. CodeQL returns, guarded for private repositories; the hardware-measure workflow is the existing `measure.yml` and is not added again. Decisions in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, entry "Raffica PDF: redaction, OCR and text editing conventions (M2.5)".

What changed during implementation against the plan of Milestone 2.5 (details in the amendment of the entry "Raffica PDF: redaction, OCR and text editing conventions (M2.5)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`): `redact-structure` and `redact-objstm` are refused by Core for unremovable page keys and not redacted (the plan text listed them as redactable); the acceptance asserts the refusal. The rescue pages (page as image) join the plan after the picker and the plan-version re-check, not before. Text marks are built as `Kind.Text` marks directly. The retry for a full OCR history was dropped because Core writes the result anyway and reports `Undoable = false`; the app words OCR failures through the new Core type `OcrFailure` because it may not reference `Raffica.Ocr`. Ctrl+Shift+G toggles the whole-line switch of the text-edit field. `ocr.languages` is locked while a run goes, and the recognize card has a "current page" option. Added beyond the plan: `ModeExclusion.CanStart` (the one exception Annotate then Organize), the original-file arming for every alias of the open file, `SetOverlayStyle`, and `AnnotationHistory.HasLiveTextEdits` in Core.

Published-size budgets of the PDF app raised (owner decision, 2026-11-06): the CI size check of the PR failed at 65.33 MiB on Windows and 64.65 MiB on Linux because the OCR library and the bundled English and German language data are now part of the package. The owner chose to count them: size 66 and zip 29 MiB on Windows, size 65 and zip 30 MiB on Linux (limits budget x 1.25); every other budget is unchanged. Entry "Raffica PDF: published size budgets after the OCR payload (M2.5)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.
`TitleBar.Trailing`, a new additive slot of the shell's title bar, hosts the update button of the PDF app; no existing shell API changed.

The update test vector was regenerated with a throwaway key and the Raffica names (the Pagewing vector cannot verify here); the key was deleted afterwards. The test build (`-p:RafficaUpdateTestBuild=true`, `RafficaUpdateTestPort`, `RafficaUpdateTestKey`) exists only for the smokes and is never set by a release.

Imported from Pagewing `v1.0.0` in one unchanged commit and renamed, translated and trimmed in the next: `tools/package.cs`, `tools/licenses.cs`, `tools/update-testserver.cs`, `tools/smoke-cli.cs`, `packaging/windows`, `packaging/linux` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Left out: `check-binary` and `native-fetch` of the old `package.cs` (this repository has its own `tools/check-binary.cs` and `tools/native-fetch.cs`). Entry "Raffica PDF: packaging and release (M2.6)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.

No Raffica mark exists yet, so a generated placeholder icon is used in the installer, as the icon resource of `RafficaPdf.exe` (`ApplicationIcon` in `Raffica.Pdf.csproj`, the same `.ico` as the installer) and in the Linux packages (`tools/make-placeholder-icon.cs`, `Docs/design/icons/`); the owner supplies the real mark and overwrites the placeholder files (Open items j). Pagewing artwork was not reused.

The placeholder icon is replaced by the brand marks the owner supplied: `Docs/design/icons/brand/` holds one master per app (`suite`, `write`, `sheets`, `slides`, `pdf`), and the PDF mark is the `.ico` of the installer and of `RafficaPdf.exe` and the hicolor PNGs of the Linux packages. `tools/make-placeholder-icon.cs` is removed. The other four marks are not packaged until their apps exist. Open items h is reduced to a look at the icon on real machines.

A release-readiness review on 2026-11-08 (eight independent reviews of security, bugs and UI, a live UI test on Windows, and a Linux measurement over its limits) found one blocker (fork pull requests could reach the self-hosted release runners once the repository is public) and several high findings (redaction kept page attachments, dead start tiles, a ribbon that hides commands at the default size, editable combo fields without a text box). Milestone 2.7 "Release readiness" is added before the first release; the owner chose on 2026-11-08 to give every command its own icon before `v0.1.0`, to move CI to hosted runners once public, and to show only "Open PDF" on the start view until the other apps exist.

The owner closes 2.6 with the default-app registration on real Windows and Linux desktops (Open items e), the per-machine update with a real UAC prompt (i) and the update path with the real signing key (a) not verified, and decides to skip the real-desktop default-app check for now. Acceptance criterion 2 is ticked with the Windows and Linux self-updates through the real window as its evidence and with these exceptions written into its evidence; the items stay listed under Open items and are checked at or after the first release.

A third-party inventory (`third-party/licenses.json`, checked by `tools/licenses.cs`) with the license texts imported verbatim from Pagewing `v1.0.0` and the AppImage runtime texts was added, and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` is generated from it for every package and the About card. The plan did not list it, but the About card and `licenses.cs check` need it.

`PdfOptions` gained `--register-file-types=user|machine`, `--unregister-file-types=user|machine`, `--finish-update <staging>`, `--after-process <pid>` and `--restore-session`: the updater restarts the new version with the session of the old one, which nobody had implemented (tabs reopen in order, the last one active; the view per tab is not restored).
`UpdateServices.MeasurementKeepsUpdatesOff` keeps the update check and the default-app offer off in the measurement runs (`--measure-*`), so the numbers of 2.1 stay comparable.
The About card shows the notices in sections (one toggle per component, text created on first open) instead of one text box: the single 467,290-character box froze the card for 0.4 to 1.4 s.

An install refuses with a worded note (`UpdateBusyNote`, `PdfWindow.InstallUpdateAsync`) while a file job runs, and asks about unsaved changes in every tab first (`UpdateInstallGuard`); the progress card names each step in words and offers Cancel only up to the check step.

The card "Set Raffica as default for PDFs?" remembers "Not now" for 30 days (`AppSettings.DefaultAppPromptSnoozedUntil`, `DefaultAppFlow`) instead of returning at every start; the card is offered again on the first start after that day. "Don't ask again" stays permanent. This changes the behavior of Milestone 2.6 (once per start), found as a repeated nuisance in the review of 2026-11-08 (08-UI-16).

Milestones 3.1 "Runs on the Mac", 3.2 "Feels like a Mac app" and 3.3 "Package and release" are added under the macOS spec. They cover both `osx-x64` and `osx-arm64`; Apple silicon is released with automatic checks only and marked "not tested by hand" in the README. Decisions: "Raffica on macOS: scope and Mac conventions (M3)" and "Raffica on macOS: speed checks and CI (M3)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.
Milestone 4 (Spikes & spec for Raffica Write) now depends on 3.3 instead of 3, so that "macOS before Write" stays true after the macOS spec milestone.

The backlog entry "Option key handling on macOS" is decided (no key tips and no Option capture on macOS, see "Raffica on macOS: scope and Mac conventions (M3)") and moves into milestone 3.2. The backlog entry "macOS print panel" is added; printing on macOS uses the own print card over CUPS.

A throwaway `packaging/macos/dev-app.sh` wraps a publish folder into an ad-hoc signed `.app` for the owner's manual Finder check. The spec puts `Info.plist` and the bundle into 3.3, but the check of 3.1 (Finder double-click and `open -a`) needs a bundle; 3.3 replaces the script by the real bundle step.

`native-tesseract.yml` gets a `systems` input (`macos`, besides the existing platforms) so that the macOS libraries are built as their own release `native-tesseract-5.5.4-2` and the Windows and Linux pins and release `-1` stay as they are. See "Raffica on macOS: native libraries, paths and activation (M3.1)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.
`UserDataPaths.CacheDirectory` (`~/Library/Caches/Raffica` on macOS) is added although nothing consumes it yet, because the task names the cache folder; the first consumer decides its use.

The task "App life cycle without windows" moves the window life cycle (Finder files, Dock reopen, quit and the next window) to `WindowHost`, but the update flow and the dialog queue stay on `PdfWindow` and come back with each new window (a ready update is dropped with its window), and the single-instance listener moved to the host on macOS only (Windows and Linux keep it on the window). Making them app-wide is a bigger change with no gain until Write shares a host; see `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "Raffica on macOS: menu bar, keys and life cycle (M3.2)". Recognize text moves from Ctrl+Shift+Q to Shift+Cmd+R on macOS only (Shift+Cmd+Q is Log Out).

`measure.yml` gets the platform `macos-hosted` (the GitHub-hosted `macos-15`, Apple silicon, `osx-arm64`): it produces the CSVs, the summary and the artifact `measure-macos-hosted-<run_id>` and has no check step, so its numbers are recorded without a limit; the owner's Intel Mac stays the platform `macos`.

`build-macos` also bundles and smokes: for both architectures it runs `macos-app`, the Mach-O check, the command line smoke, `dmg` and `dmg-smoke`, and, since the sizes were recorded, `size --check` against the one `macos` budget entry (size, zip, app, dmg; that step has not run in CI since the switch).

`RAFFICA_RENDERING=software` also selects software rendering on macOS (`AvaloniaNativeRenderingMode.Software`); it is opt-in only and the macOS default is unchanged until the Intel measurement of `measure.yml` decides (open, the Mac runner was offline).

tessdata lives in `Contents/Resources/tessdata` of the bundle, not in `Contents/MacOS`, because `codesign` treats a folder in `Contents/MacOS` as a nested code component; `TessdataStore.ShippedDirectoryFor` finds it through one bundle-specific rule (`Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "Raffica on macOS: packaging, default app and updates (M3.3)").

`third-party/licenses.json` owns the macOS natives (`libAvaloniaNative.dylib`, `libSkiaSharp.dylib`, `libHarfBuzzSharp.dylib`), and `tools/check-binary.cs` reads universal Mach-O files and ignores a dylib's own install name when it lists dependencies.

The size budgets of the PDF app on macOS are one `macos` entry of `s_pdfBudgets` (size, zip, app, dmg; the larger architecture binds both) and have no time or memory limit until the Intel measurement; see "Raffica PDF on macOS: published sizes and the hosted record (M3.3)" in `Docs/DECISIONS.md`.

The printing and IME spikes also cover macOS (a supported platform since milestone 3), and printing is checked as Write printing itself (Windows draws directly onto the printer, Linux and macOS hand CUPS a PDF in memory), not through Raffica PDF; see the spike design `superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-raffica-write-spikes-design.md`.

milestones.title: Repo skeleton & CI
milestones.goal: A set-up repo with the renamed Pagewing core, tests and CI on which all further milestones build.

tasks.text: Create the spec (brainstorming): goal, scope, stack, subprojects; link it here and enter the first milestones
Repo setup done: `dev` as default branch, merge options, branch protection for `main` and `dev`
Fill in the project header of `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`, remove the template section from the README
Import commit 1: the Pagewing core (`Core`, `Pdfium`, `Ocr`, `Cli`), its tests, test data and licence files from the `v1.0.0` tag, unchanged, with a stack-specific `.gitignore`
Import commit 2: scripted rename (dry run first), updater keys and URLs replaced by documented placeholders
Make the subset self-contained and green: solution file, removal of App-coupled tests, OCR library fetch script, `.editorconfig`; project skeleton incl. test projects
Translate the imported German comments, strings and test names to English
`.env.example` with placeholders, if secrets are needed (not needed, see scope change)
CI (GitHub Actions): build, test and format/lint on PRs to `dev` and `main`; the job `roadmap` from `.github/workflows/roadmap.yml` stays; aggregate check `ci`
Record the build, test and format/lint commands in `CLAUDE.md` and write the README setup section
Enter the CI jobs (`roadmap` and `ci`) as required status checks in the branch protection of `main` and `dev` (only on the owner's explicit instruction)

blocks.title: Open items
blocks.text:
**2.6 was closed by the owner on 2026-11-08 with the items below still open** (as 2.1 to 2.4 were). The code, tests, packaging tools and the release workflow are done; criteria 1 and 3 are ticked with the dry run (run 42422270038, https://github.com/benjo-code/raffica/actions/runs/42422270038); criterion 2 is ticked with the Windows and Linux self-updates through the real window (runs 42500189081 and 42494883539) and with the default-app registration on real desktops, the per-machine update with a real UAC prompt and the path with the real key explicitly not verified (Open items e, i and a).

**What was done and verified here (Windows, commit eafe91c, 2026-11-07).**
- `dotnet build Raffica.slnx -c Release`: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `RAFFICA_REQUIRE_OCR=1 dotnet test Raffica.slnx -c Release --no-build --max-parallel-test-modules 1`: 5777 total, 0 failed, 31 skipped (Linux-only, CUPS and measurement-only tests); `dotnet format Raffica.slnx --verify-no-changes`: clean; `dotnet run tools/roadmap.cs -- check`: valid.
- `dotnet publish src/Raffica.Pdf/Raffica.Pdf.csproj -c Release -r win-x64`: 0 warnings, 68.48 MiB without `.pdb` files (`RafficaPdf.exe` 36,132,864 bytes); `RafficaPdf.exe --print-string TabView --lang de` printed `Ansicht`.
- Windows packages for real: `package.cs layout`, `zip`, `installer` and `installer-smoke` ("all steps passed": first install, second install over it, uninstall, keys and folder gone, `%APPDATA%\Raffica` unchanged). Windows update chain with the TEST key: `package.cs update-smoke` 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 "through the helper mode passed". `package.cs selftest` 599 checks passed on Windows (622 on Linux in the dry run), `licenses.cs selftest` 42 checks passed, `licenses.cs check` ok.
- Measured published size (task 7, before the About card sections): 68.32 MiB (budget 66, limit 82.5) and zip 29.5 MiB (budget 29, limit 36.25).
- **Release workflow dry run (`dev` commit 4a31a74b81563f6015dc773ebe07a7b12ab16ca9, run 42422270038):** `release-preflight`, `release-windows` (ZIP with 13 files, installer, `installer-smoke: all steps passed`) and `release-linux` (selftest 622 checks passed, container build, `.deb`, AppImage, smokes) green, `release-manifest` skipped as designed; nothing uploaded. The first dry run (run 42418844306 on 841cfd6) had failed in `release-linux` at the Linux-only part of the packaging selftest (a stale fixture path `Raffica PDF` instead of `RafficaPdf`; fixed by PR #37).
- **Linux packages built for real in Docker (ubuntu:22.04, Linux SDK 10.0.403, clean `git archive` export) before the dry run.** The build found and fixed three defects in the packaging code: commit ae05f31 (the glibc check now allows `libfontconfig.so.1` of Skia through a new `--allow-needed` option of `tools/check-binary.cs`), commit 422c5b5 (the AppImage smoke passed no `--settings-file`) and commit ed6caba (the AppImage smoke waited for `first-sharp` instead of `first-page`). Then green end to end: glibc check ok for `RafficaPdf`, `libHarfBuzzSharp`, `libSkiaSharp`, `libpdfium` (app and cli), `cli/raffica` and `libtesseract`; layout 12 files; `.deb` 21 entries (`/usr/bin/raffica` and `/usr/bin/raffica-pdf` links, `/usr/lib/raffica-pdf/*`, the desktop file, hicolor icons 16 to 512, copyright); `deb-smoke` passed; `desktop-file-validate` code 0; lintian errors only of the classes the smoke accepts (`embedded-library`, `no-changelog`, `unstripped-binary-or-object`; warning `no-manual-page`); `.deb` 30,894,280 bytes, AppImage 32,864,760 bytes, `fuse-3.15.0.tar.xz` 4,589,124, `type2-runtime-20251108.tar.gz` 31,045, `SHA256SUMS-linux.txt` 374; `appimage-smoke` under xvfb passed (the app draws `text-basic.pdf`, `first-page`, exit 0 with `APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1`; without the variable the container has no FUSE and the runtime says so, which the smoke accepts as designed). MIME handling is `MimeType=application/pdf;` in the desktop file only.
- **On real Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 container):** `AppImageUpdaterTests` 10 of 10 passed (including the Mode755 assertion that is skipped on Windows). The real window class under Xvfb with no window manager: `xprop WM_CLASS` returns "RafficaPdf", "RafficaPdf", so `StartupWMClass=RafficaPdf` matches on X11 (the Wayland app_id was not tested).
- **Lessons of the real runs:** a Windows-only `package.cs selftest` does not cover its Linux part (the first dry run found the stale fixture path), and the packaging code needed a real Linux build to be right (the three defects above).

**Open items (each with the command or check).**
- **a. The real update key (partly done, 2026-11-08).** The key `release-1` exists, its private half is the secret `RAFFICA_UPDATE_SIGNING_KEY` of the environment `release-signing` (set by the owner), and its public half replaced the placeholder in `src/Raffica.Core/Updates/UpdateTrust.cs` (`package.cs update-verify --keys-from-source` exits 0, the update tests pass with `RAFFICA_REQUIRE_RELEASE_KEY=1`). Still open: the update path with the real key is unproven until the first signed release exists (criterion 2).
- **b. Environment and visibility.** The environment `release-signing` exists with the secret; the required reviewer and the branch policy cannot be set while the repository is private on the owner's plan, so add both as soon as the repository is public (check with `gh api repos/benjo-code/raffica/environments/release-signing`) and before the first `upload=true` run. Making the repository public (`gh repo edit benjo-code/raffica --visibility public`) is the owner's action and was not run.
- **c. The first release.** The number (for example `v0.1.0`) and the owner's go; the commands are in `CLAUDE.md` ("Releases") and `packaging/README.md`: `gh release create vX.Y.Z --target main ...` then `gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f tag=vX.Y.Z -f upload=true`. The dry run is green (run 42422270038), but the `upload=true` path with the real key and the job `release-manifest` has not run. No update is offered before the first release exists.
- **d. Linux on a real desktop (part of criterion 2).** Done on 2026-11-08 on the owner's CachyOS laptop (KDE Plasma, Wayland, real FUSE mount): the AppImage self-update 0.0.1 to 0.0.2 against the test server with the throw-away test key, by the workflow `linux-update-check.yml` (run 42494883539, https://github.com/benjo-code/raffica/actions/runs/42494883539): the file is the new AppImage (SHA-256), mode 755, no leftover file, a new process started from it, the new file starts through FUSE; by eye the owner saw the update offered, installed, the new version open with the PDF back, and the About card showing 0.0.2 (test build). An earlier run (42494168938) was red because the script reported the app as closed although the owner saw the update work; the script now prints diagnostics and checks the file once more, and the cause of that red run was not found (a script flake, not seen again). Still open: `sudo apt install ./raffica-pdf_<v>_amd64.deb`, open a PDF, `sudo apt remove raffica-pdf` on a Debian or Ubuntu machine; the window class on Wayland (`app_id`) against `StartupWMClass=RafficaPdf`.
- **e. Default app on real systems.** Windows 11: Settings, Default apps, Raffica PDF; Linux desktop: `xdg-mime query default application/pdf`. Only a sandbox registry key, fake runners and the settings URI opener were exercised.
- **f. Printers** (carried over from 2.1): real printers, CUPS and the Win32 dialog; `CupsPrintServiceTests` run with `RAFFICA_TEST_CUPS_PRINTER`.
- **g. SmartScreen and Authenticode.** The installer has no Authenticode signature, so Windows shows a warning; the README says so. Check by downloading the installer through a browser on a clean Windows machine.
- **h. Icons (done, 2026-11-08).** The brand marks are in `Docs/design/icons/brand/` and the exe, the installer and the packages carry the PDF mark (`Docs/design/icons/README.md`). Still to look at on a real machine: the icon of the installed exe, of the Start menu entry and of PDF files in Explorer, and the Linux menu entry.
- **i. A real UAC prompt.** The update helper was run per-user only; a per-machine install update with a real elevation prompt (and a declined prompt) is not exercised.
- **j. Size and speed budgets.** The published size 68.32 MiB (68.48 MiB after the About sections) is over the 66 MiB budget and under the 82.5 MiB limit; the budget needs the owner's decision (the size check is the CI step "Size of the published PDF app" and `dotnet run bench/shell-probe/measure.cs -- size --check win-x64 --target pdf --publish-dir <dir> ...`). The time budgets and idle memory (38.62 MiB private bytes with the update flow off, 39.23 MiB with it on against the loopback server, an estimated about 39.4 MiB with the real check, against the budget of 40 MiB; headroom thin) need the owner's machines: `gh workflow run measure.yml --ref <branch> -f platform=windows -f target=pdf -f note="<machine>"`.
- **k. About card.** The three largest notice sections (the PDFium and HarfBuzz native bundles and the .NET runtime notice) take 0.2 to 0.4 s on their first expand; the closed list and the other sections are fast. The cheap next step is to page those three. Check on a real display by opening About and expanding each section.
- **l. Flaky tests seen in CI (each green on re-run; watch).** (1) The test host crash with a `NullReferenceException` in `Avalonia.Threading.Dispatcher.RequestProcessing`, called from a scheduler or session callback on a pool thread (`PageView.OnPagesInvalidated`, `PagesPane.OnTileReady`; once in CI, run 42419846708). Addressed in PR #38 (merged): handlers and timer or progress callbacks that run on pool threads no longer touch the static `Dispatcher.UIThread`, they post through the dispatcher their owner captured on the UI thread, and `TextEditSession` keeps its flush synchronous on the UI thread. The cause was derived from the stack trace and the Avalonia 12.1.5 source and not reproduced (every headless test has its own dispatcher and the end of a test clears the static one; a late callback of a leftover window would make a new dispatcher on the pool thread, published before its platform part is set, and a second poster would throw); `TeardownRaceTests` pins only PagesPane, PageView and OrganizeList. Confirm by watching CI; the real app is not affected. (2) `Raffica.Core.Tests.Ocr.OcrRunnerTests.PdfiumThreadIsNeverBlockedByRecognition` failed once on the shared Windows runner (`Assert.True(clock.ElapsedMilliseconds < 200 ...)` with 667 ms): a timing assertion on a loaded runner; Core code was untouched by that PR and the check was not changed. The owner decides whether to leave it, widen it or move it to the measurement-only tests.

backlog.title: Security hardening left from the pass of 2026-11-12
backlog.text: The security pass of 2026-11-12 (read-only review of the macOS code and the workflows) found nothing high; these are the hardening items that were left. **Update chain:** the extracted macOS bundle is not pinned to the signed manifest (only `codesign --verify --deep --strict` and the file hash of the image; the staged bundle sits next to the installed app until the swap), so hash the image again after `ditto` and put the bundle's CDHash into the signed manifest; a signed manifest has no sequence number or minimum version, so someone who can write the GitHub release could point `latest` at an older signed release that is still newer than the installed one; a swap script that is killed between its two moves leaves the app hidden in `.Raffica PDF previous.app` without a log, so write a log line and restore the backup at the next start. **Mach-O check:** `MachORules` does not read `LC_RPATH` (`otool -l`: accept only `@loader_path` and `@executable_path`). **Workflows:** `measure.yml` and the two update-check workflows accept any branch of the repository as `ref` on the owner's self-hosted machines (apply the rule of `release.yml`: the commit is on `main` or `dev`); `release.yml` tests tag and ref with `$` where `\z` is exact; `measure.yml` should pass `reference_project` through `env`.

backlog.title: Release readiness follow-ups (from M2.7)
backlog.text: Known limits of 2.7 that were recorded, not fixed. **Accessibility:** the page view exposes no page text to screen readers (it is a picture); the high-contrast mode uses the app's own palette, not the system colours; no Narrator or NVDA pass was made (the automation names and patterns are pinned by tests only); the disclosure rows of the About card lack an ExpandCollapse peer; the tab strip arrow loses keyboard focus when it is disabled at the end of the strip. **Layout:** the Alt key tips of some small buttons overlap a neighbouring icon; Undo and Redo are only on the Start tab; the scroll chevrons of the ribbon never show in the PDF app at 1024 px because the auto-compact layout fits first; the window `MinWidth` could be lower; the tab list flyout has no `MaxHeight` for 50 and more tabs. **Icons:** a simplified 16 px variant of the Lucide icons for the compact bar. **Code:** the `JobRunner` and `SaveController` progress posts run at default dispatcher priority; the `AboutCard` title test only restates the string. **From the final review of 2026-11-09 (unverified, a guess about PDFium and Avalonia):** `PdfiumPageText` loads one PDFium page per distinct link target on every link read, which may be slow on a contents page of a long document; the held-Enter guard of `Dialog` can stay set when the key-up goes to a native file picker that was opened with Enter, so Enter would stop working in that card; the end of an error loop calls `desktop.Shutdown(1)`, and what that does with unsaved tabs is not tested; `FileIdentity.AreSameFile` gives no answer on a Linux without `statx`, which makes the open-target guard refuse every write while a second tab is open; `CrashGuard.Scrub` does not cover a forward-slash UNC path or every Linux root. **Owner checks that need real hardware:** the real display, Narrator or NVDA, an IME and an AltGr layout (see the live pass of 2026-11-09).

backlog.title: Clean up references to Pagewing documents and translate the fixture catalogue
backlog.text: About 68 imported files cite Pagewing's German decision-log entries or `packaging/README.md` in comments; the references point at documents that are not in this repo. `testdata/pdfs/LICENSES.md` is still German and describes fixtures generated by `tools/make-testpdfs.cs`, which was not imported. Replace the references with Raffica entries or drop them, translate the catalogue, and decide whether to import or rebuild the test PDF generator.

backlog.title: Macros and extensions
backlog.text: A macro and extension system (a VBA replacement), someday, not for the beginning.

backlog.title: Real-time collaboration
backlog.text: Several people editing one document at the same time, someday, not for the beginning.

backlog.title: What the field-code group numbers should do
backlog.text: In field-code mode the group digits are shown as a legend only; Q, 6 and 7 act. Decide whether typing a group digit should do something (for example jump to the group).

backlog.title: German wording for "System" in the settings dialog
backlog.text: The German label "Wie System" (`SettingsThemeSystem`, the follow-the-system theme choice) needs the owner's decision on the wording.

backlog.title: Ctrl+K and hyperlinks in Write
backlog.text: The frame binds Ctrl+K to the search field. Word and other editors use Ctrl+K for inserting a hyperlink; settle this in the Write spec (note for the Write spec).

backlog.title: Accessibility items deferred from the frame
backlog.text: Not done in milestone 1.2: the selected state of ribbon tabs is not exposed to assistive technology (only a style class; the document tabs expose it since milestone 2.1), the search results list has no selection semantics, and a document tab has two tab stops (tab and close button).

backlog.title: macOS print panel
backlog.text: Print through the native macOS print panel (Preview, PDF export, presets) instead of the app's own CUPS print card. Left out of subproject 4 because it needs Objective-C interop for NSPrintOperation; the own card over CUPS is the decided path (spec 5.6).

backlog.title: Tabs between windows and open in a new window
backlog.text: Pagewing 1.0 let a tab be moved to its own window (menu "Open in new window", M4) and dragged between windows (M4.1, Windows only). Raffica PDF 2.1 has one window with tabs; the frame's `DocumentTabs` has no drag-out. Revisit after 2.6 or when the owner asks.

backlog.title: Setting "reduce animations"
backlog.text: Pagewing 1.0 had it in the settings (M6, because Avalonia had no system setting for it). Raffica's shell has no such setting; add it as an extra row of the settings dialog or as a shell setting once the shell has animations that matter.

backlog.title: Remove the overlap between Core and Shell settings
backlog.text: Core's `AppSettings` still has `Theme`, `Language` and `Density`, which the shell settings (`ShellSettings`) own; the PDF app does not read them. Remove the fields or migrate them so that two files cannot disagree.

backlog.title: PDF app: command states and icons
backlog.text: Toggle commands (dark page, panes) have no checked state; add a shell `CheckedWhen` like `EnabledWhen`. Missing shell icons: printer, gear, up and left chevrons, moon, copy; the ribbon uses the least misleading placeholders. Disabled ribbon buttons are not focusable, so the reason (for example for print) shows on hover only; expose it as help text.

backlog.title: PDF app: pane and print card accessibility
backlog.text: The outline is a flat list with depth in the automation name, not a tree with levels in the accessibility tree; there is no visible pane switcher (ribbon group and shortcuts switch); the print job card has no live region or real progress element.

backlog.title: Print follow-ups
backlog.text: Cancelling during the CUPS submit still prints (the submit call, cupsPrintFile2, cannot be cancelled and the app does not call cupsCancelJob2 afterwards: add it and test it on a Linux machine, see DECISIONS, viewer deviations). Failed pages are lost if the job is cancelled afterwards.

backlog.title: Search and selection follow-ups
backlog.text: The selection highlight is lost when Core's page-text cache (32 pages) evicts a page. An unhandled `TileFailed` leaves a page on its preview.

backlog.title: Speed follow-ups of the viewer
backlog.text: Read `recent.json` in parallel with the first open so that a command-line file opens at its remembered position (about 2 ms per run). Per-frame allocations in `PageView.Replan` and `DrawPage` (a `Pen` per page, LINQ in the planner) are small on the dev VM; re-check the scroll case on real GPU machines before changing them.

backlog.title: Annotate keys: possible latent routing problem (M2.2)
backlog.text: `AnnotateInteraction` uses a bubble handler gated on `!Handled`, so the arrow keys of a selected mark may be consumed by `PageView`'s class handler first. The redact mode had exactly this bug in M2.5 and uses a tunnel handler now. Check the annotate mode with a routed key test (a real key event through the window) before changing anything.

backlog.title: OCR run lock is window-wide
backlog.text: `OcrBusy` disables Save and Print in every tab while a text-recognition run goes, not only in the tab that is being recognized. It is the existing design of the busy lists; a per-tab rule needs the save and print flows to ask the tab.

backlog.title: Redaction of files with unremovable page keys
backlog.text: Any file with `/Thumb`, `/PieceInfo`, `/Metadata` or `/AA` on any page is refused by Core and gets no rescue (`redact-structure`, `redact-objstm`). Turning the offending page into an image would drop the keys but is a design question for the owner: which pages may be turned into pictures without asking, and what the card says.

backlog.title: Redaction analysis time for 1000 pages (13.8 s measured)
backlog.text: The analysis step before the Apply card took 13.8 s for `thousand-pages.pdf` with one area mark per page, and the rewrite and check 15.2 s (single run, see `Docs/DECISIONS.md`, "... measurements (M2.5)"). Look at what the analysis does per page (reading and measuring every page) and whether it can skip unmarked pages; re-measure on the owner's machines first.

backlog.title: Run the native build workflow again after a version bump
backlog.text: Steps: bump the versions in the build files (`versions.txt`), dispatch `.github/workflows/native-tesseract.yml` (`gh workflow run native-tesseract.yml -f build=1`, the workflow must exist on the default branch), copy the sizes and SHA-256 of the job summary into the pins of `tools/native-fetch.cs`, update the tests that name them, run `dotnet run tools/native-fetch.cs -- selftest` and the OCR tests with `RAFFICA_REQUIRE_OCR=1`. Running it is an owner gate.

backlog.title: Predecessor's open items worth keeping
backlog.text: From the predecessor's M14 to M16 designs and not built in 2.5: a code list of overlay text ("blocks") for repeated labels; `/Redact` annotation markers so marks survive a save before Apply; QPDF post-processing of the written file; OSD and deskew for OCR; removing an imported language file from the app; reuse of the embedded replacement font for edited text; keep-lists for bookmarks and forms that point into redacted pages.

backlog.title: Text edit: vertical lines, field rotation, Tab across unloaded pages
backlog.text: The text edit mode does not handle vertical writing, sizes the field for rotated pages only approximately, and Tab walks only the pages whose runs are loaded (the focus never jumps over an unloaded page). Ctrl+Shift+G is not in the command catalog or the help card, so it is announced only when the switch changes.

backlog.title: A dedicated OCR permission reason
backlog.text: The gate of `ocr.run` for a locked file reuses the wording of the annotate lock ("annotations"); give it its own reason text in both languages.

backlog.title: Print with pending redaction marks prints the unredacted pages
backlog.text: Plan call 2 says "Print stays" in the redact mode, so a print while marks are pending prints the pages as they are, without the marks applied. Owner decision: add a note on the print card while marks are pending (and say what is printed), or lock print like Save.

backlog.title: Native build workflow: split build and upload permissions
backlog.text: `.github/workflows/native-tesseract.yml` has three jobs and all of them hold `contents: write`. Give the build jobs `contents: read` and keep `contents: write` for the upload step only so the third-party source builds without a write token, and fix the header comment that names a `release.yml` that does not exist.

backlog.title: Scan hint reappears after a redact or organize rebuild
backlog.text: `PdfTab.ResetForRewrittenDocument` drops `ScanHintHandled`, so "Not now" and "Don't ask again for this file" are forgotten after an Apply that rebuilds the tab. Keep the flag for the same file across the rebuild.

backlog.title: TextEditSession.cs is 939 lines
backlog.text: `src/Raffica.Pdf/TextEditing/TextEditSession.cs` holds the runs, the draft, the preview and the commit. Split candidate: the commit and the old-text note from the reading of the runs.

backlog.title: Duplicated preamble of the mode starters
backlog.text: `ToggleOrganizeAsync`, `ToggleRedactAsync`, `ToggleTextEditAsync` and `StartOcrRunAsync` repeat the same preamble (flush an open field edit and a typed comment of the marks pane, re-check the locks afterwards). Extract one helper with a test per mode.

backlog.title: Marks pane comment field when Edit text starts
backlog.text: `OnPlanChanged` of the marks pane is hooked to the Organize and OCR sessions but not to `TextEditSession`. A comment field that is still shown when Edit text starts stays editable on screen, but `ApplyCommentAsync` returns early because `PlanLocked` is true, so text typed there is silently not applied (choosing and deleting a mark are correctly blocked). Re-evaluate the lock, and the read-only state of the field, when the text edit session changes.

backlog.title: Flaky macOS UI tests on the hosted runner
backlog.text: Two macOS UI tests each failed once in earlier `build-macos` attempts of milestone 3.3 and passed on a re-run: `OrganizeListTests.FocusStaysOnItsRowAfterSelectAllAndMoves` and `TextEditRobustnessTests.EmptyTextThroughEnterInTheRealWindowRemovesTheLineAndUndoBringsItBack`. Whether they were flaky before 3.3 was not examined (not proven pre-existing). Look for a focus or dispatcher timing dependence on the hosted `macos-15` runner and fix the test or the code; do not skip them. Seen since: `TextEditKeysTests.EnterCommitsEscDiscardsTabLeavesAndNeverTraps` failed once on the first `build-macos` attempt of PR #72 (`Assert.NotNull` at the text-edit field) and passed on the re-run; `WindowHostWindowTests.QuitRequestedIsClearedByACancelledAttempt` failed once in a full local run on Windows (`DirtyTabAsync`, an assertion that the tab is dirty) and passed three times alone.

backlog.title: RenderSchedulerTests.InvalidatePagesDoesNotWaitForARunningHandler can kill the test process
backlog.text: On the Windows job of PR #75 the `Raffica.Core.Tests` run ended with an unhandled `ObjectDisposedException` ('System.Threading.ManualResetEventSlim') and exit code -532462766; a re-run passed. The stack is the test's own handler (`RenderSchedulerTests.InvalidatePagesDoesNotWaitForARunningHandler`, a lambda that waits on a `ManualResetEventSlim`) called by `RenderScheduler.Raise` on a pool thread, so the test disposes the event while the handler thread still waits on it; an unhandled exception on a pool thread ends the whole test host. Not a proven product bug. Make the test wait for the handler to finish (or release the event only after it) before it disposes anything, and check whether the other `RenderSchedulerTests` handlers have the same shape.
